sub1: Weekday Lates with weeks 13–17 kept exactly as written, the evening gap filled, and the fatigue factors driven as low as this design allows
h3: What was held, what moved, and what it cost
sub3: Five weeks kept to the letter; the evening filled from the two turns outside them
coverNote: gaps of 8, 6, 5, 5 around the wheel — inherited from Weekday Lates, not re-spread
methodHeading: How the factors were brought down
h7: How it was built, and how to load it
sub7: Reproducible: the same starting grid, seed and objective give the same rotation on any machine
method:
1 · Weeks 13–17 are kept to the letter. Every one of those five weeks appears in this rotation exactly as written in Weekday Lates — not a day, not a time altered. What changed is where they sit: 13, 14, 15, 16 and 17 are now lines 21, 3, 6, 24 and 1. That is the whole reason the factors could come down, and it is explained in the note opposite.

2 · The evening was filled from what was left. Nine duties ran 08:30–17:00 and all nine finished at once, which is why cover fell to six from 17:00 while December traffic peaks. Three of the nine are inside week 16 and were therefore untouchable; the rest are line 9's week and line 6's Friday, and both moved to 12:30–21:00 — 8h30, the same length, so the contracted week is still paid to the minute.

3 · Then the rotation was searched fatigue-first. Every factor present charged over and above its size, four restarts a seed, three seeds, with the two coverage-preserving moves only. Factors present fell from five to one, MRSF's 55-hour row from 58.9h to 51.1h, FF8b from five instances to none, and the longest run from nine days to six.
openQuestions: Zero was the target and one is the floor, for a reason worth understanding. The factor left is FF19 — successive start times varying by more than two hours — at three instances, down from seven. It cannot be zero in any rotation containing both early and late weeks: going round the cycle you must cross from earlies to lates and back again, and each crossing is by definition a jump of more than two hours. Three is the fewest of the three seeds; two is the arithmetic floor for a design with this mix of turns. What protecting the five weeks cost. Had they been free to be rewritten, the factor count would be the same but the rotation softer: full weekends off are 4 in 24 here against 6 in Weekday Lates, because the search had five fewer weeks to arrange around. That is the price of keeping them, and it is a real one. If they must also stay at lines 13–17, zero is not merely hard but impossible: week 13 works Tue–Sat and week 14 Sun–Mon, so pinned adjacent they form a single 58.9-hour seven-day window that nothing else in the grid can break, and MRSF's row can never clear. Moving them apart is what took it to 51.1.
